form.help.preset.title: Presets
form.help.preset.intro: A preset sets the model, both time constants and the weight of fatigue at once. Change a value afterwards and you see “Custom values”; monotony and estimate factors are not touched.
form.help.preset.classic: Fitness 42 days, fatigue 7 days, weight 1.0. Fatigue rises quickly after hard days and is gone after a few rest days; form swings clearly. Good for seeing load peaks and resting before a race.
form.help.preset.responsive: Fitness 21 days, fatigue 12 days, weight 0.75. Fitness reacts faster to more or less training, fatigue fades more slowly and counts less. Form runs calmer and rather shows the development over a few weeks.
form.help.preset.tip: Tip: try both presets and compare the curve with how you felt over the last weeks. What matters is the trend and the ratio, not the exact numbers.
form.help.model.title: Model, time constants and weight
form.help.model.intro: Every activity gives a load (from heart rate, otherwise estimated). From it two moving averages arise: fitness (slow) and fatigue (fast). Form = fitness − weight × fatigue; positive means rested, negative means tired.
form.help.model.standard: One fatigue for the whole load. Simple and suitable for most people.
form.help.model.two_curve: Fatigue is split: load below the anaerobic threshold (threshold HR, otherwise start of zone 4) and above it. Both parts fade with their own time constant. Useful if hard intervals noticeably affect you longer than easy endurance.
form.help.model.fitness: 7–120 days, typically 21–42. How long training keeps affecting fitness: after this many days a session only counts a good third. Larger = slower, calmer fitness; smaller = it rises and falls faster.
form.help.model.fatigue: 2–30 days, shorter than fitness, typically 7–14. How quickly fatigue fades. Smaller = higher swing after hard days, gone faster after rest days; larger = fatigue lasts longer.
form.help.model.parts: Two-curve only, 2–30 days each and shorter than fitness. Aerobic shorter (default 5), anaerobic longer (default 12), because hard sessions affect you longer.
form.help.model.restBonus: Two-curve only, 0–50 % (default 18). On days without any load both fatigue time constants are shortened by this share, so fatigue drops faster. 0 % = no bonus.
form.help.model.weight: 0.25–3, comma or point. How strongly fatigue enters the form; 1.0 = as strong as fitness. Smaller = form gets less negative after hard days, larger = more cautious form. Fitness and fatigue themselves do not change.
form.help.model.states: The states from “rested” to “risk of overload” depend on fixed form limits (+25, +5, −10, −30). Other time constants or another weight change how often you reach them.
form.help.foster.title: Monotony (Foster)
form.help.foster.monotony: Mean daily load of the last 7 days divided by its standard deviation. Many similarly hard days without a rest day give high values; from 2.0 the training counts as monotonous. Strain = weekly load × monotony.
form.help.foster.surcharge: When ticked, the load on days with monotony above 2.0 counts more for fatigue by the surcharge (1–50 %, e.g. 15 %). Fitness stays the same. That way form shows that uniform training is coped with less well. Without the tick, monotony is only displayed.
form.help.estimate.title: Estimate without heart rate
form.help.estimate.how: If an activity has no HR values or no HR zones are entered yet, its load is estimated from the duration: hours × value of the sport. Example: 1.5 h cycling with 50 gives 75.
form.help.estimate.scale: For comparison: an easy hour with HR gives about 50–75, a hard hour 120 and more. If you are mostly out easy, stay towards the lower end. 0 = such activities do not count at all.
form.help.estimate.recalc: Estimated activities are marked. After saving, the affected activities are recalculated in the background.
export.intro: The full export contains everything you stored in TrackCraft:
export.gpx: one GPX file per activity from the processed points, readable by Komoot, Strava and others
export.json: the data as JSON: activities, segments and routes with best times, seasons, heart rate zones, plan, goals and settings
export.noSecrets: The Garmin key and other secrets are not included. The export is not a backup and cannot be imported yet.
export.hint: The ZIP is built while downloading; your browser shows the progress. With many activities this can take a few minutes.
